title: Build Claude/Codex skills from reference examples (videos, ads you like) instead of describing them from scratch, so the AI reverse-engineers the target output

claims: A skill is a task the AI runs the exact same way every time
Describing what you like in words makes the AI guess; giving reference artifacts stops the guessing
You can give as many reference examples as you want
Outputs from reference-built skills are 'ridiculously better' than from-scratch skills
how_to_steps: Decide the skill's job (e.g. editing videos, writing ads)
Collect real examples of the output you want (videos edited the way you like, ads you admire)
Give the examples to the AI with notes on what you like and dislike about each
Ask it to reverse-engineer them into a skill ('I want to make a skill out of this type of ad')
Add more references over time to tighten the skill
on_screen_only: Title card 'THE RIGHT WAY TO BUILD AI SKILLS'
'What's an AI skill?' with a SKILL.md file graphic next to Claude and ChatGPT logos
'Not like this' example prompt: 'Hey, I want to make this skill about editing videos.'
'Find a video you like' row of thumbnails labelled ONLINE; 'As many as you want' with an infinity symbol labelled REFERENCES
Final bar chart 'Your output: FROM SCRATCH (short bar) vs FROM REFERENCES (long bar)'

relevance.why: A simple, correct principle (few-shot from real artifacts) for anyone writing skills; Haji already builds skills so the value is a reminder, not a discovery

implement_score.why: Zero cost: when creating a skill, drop 3-5 reference artifacts into the skill folder or prompt and have Claude derive the rules. Pairs with the skill-creator workflow already in use

verify: No evidence beyond assertion that reference-built skills outperform; test on one skill with an A/B

gap.what: Technique: seed skills with reference artifacts and like/dislike notes rather than descriptions; liked set listed many skill repos but not this authoring method
